hints: Focus on how the units of Kp come from the partial pressures on the top and bottom of the expression.
Count the total moles of gas on each side, for example in the first reaction you have 2 moles on the left and 2 moles on the right.
Look for the reaction where the top and bottom pressures cancel completely, leaving a change in gas moles of zero.
walkthrough:
**Recall how Kp units work**

Kp is built from partial pressures, so its units depend on how many pressures are multiplied on top versus bottom.

$$\text{units of } K_p = (\text{pressure})^{\Delta n} \text{ where } \Delta n = \text{moles of product gas} - \text{moles of reactant gas}$$

**Calculate change in gas moles for each reaction**

Just count gas molecules on each side. This is quick and tells you everything.

$$A: \Delta n = 2 - (1+1) = 0$$
$$B: \Delta n = 2 - (3+1) = -2$$
$$C: \Delta n = 1 - 2 = -1$$
$$D: \Delta n = 2 - (2+1) = -1$$

**Pick the reaction with cancelling units**

Only when $\Delta n = 0$ do all the pressure units cancel out to leave no units. That happens when the total gas moles are the same on both sides.

options.A: For $\text{H}_2(g) + \text{I}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}(g)$, $K_p = p_{HI}^2 / (p_{H2} \times p_{I2})$. Top has $(pressure)^2$ and bottom has $(pressure)^2$, so units cancel completely. With $\Delta n = 0$, Kp has no units.
options.B: For $3\text{H}_2 + \text{N}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$, $K_p = p_{NH3}^2 / (p_{H2}^3 \times p_{N2})$. This gives $(pressure)^{-2}$, e.g. $atm^{-2}$ or $Pa^{-2}$. Students who forget to count all 4 reactant moles often miss this.
options.C: For $2\text{NO}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, $K_p = p_{N2O4} / p_{NO2}^2$. This gives $(pressure)^{-1}$, e.g. $atm^{-1}$. It is tempting because it looks simple, but the moles change from 2 to 1.
options.D: For $2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$, $K_p = p_{SO3}^2 / (p_{SO2}^2 \times p_{O2})$. This gives $(pressure)^{-1}$, e.g. $atm^{-1}$. The 2 and 2 cancel in appearance, but the extra $\text{O}_2$ leaves $\Delta n = -1$.
